headline: On last trading day, Sensex and Nifty snapped four-week winning streak amid profit booking and rising crude oil.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 30 November.

why: Profit booking pulled markets down on Friday, snapping a mid-week recovery.
Brent crude oil prices topped $97 per barrel, pressuring overall investor sentiment.
Mutual funds sold Rs 32,740 crore worth of equities so far in November.
Drag in IT stocks and major heavyweights offset earlier weekly gains.
whatHappening: Sensex and Nifty ended in the red, breaking their four-week winning streak.
TCS led weekly gains among Nifty constituents, while Tata Steel lagged.
Mutual funds raised stakes in select smallcaps like CarTrade Tech and Jaiprakash Power Ventures despite steep annual plunges.
RBI stepped up gold loan scrutiny following signals of borrower stress from bullion rout.
summary: Indian benchmark indices snapped a four-week winning streak as Sensex and Nifty ended in the red on Friday amid profit booking and elevated Brent crude prices above $97. TCS led weekly gains while Tata Steel lagged among majors. Mutual funds remained net sellers in November, unloading Rs 32,740 crore of equities.
